newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-GERMANY LOOKING TO END IRISH JINX.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMANY LOOKING TO END IRISH JINX.

text.p: European champions Germany will have to overcome a 19-year jinx and the absence of several key players if they are to beat Northern Ireland in one of 18 World Cup qualifiers being played around the continent this weekend.
While Saturday's group nine match in Nuremburg should provide Germany with three points, Northern Ireland have a surprisingly good record against the Germans.
They have won two and drawn two of their last four matches against them and have not lost to them since 1977 when current German manager Berti Vogts was still playing.
Anything other than a German victory would be seen as a major upset. The Irish have made a disappointing start to their campaign with one defeat and one draw at home against Ukraine and Armenia.

Although the Germans will be without injured libero Matthias Sammer, defender Thomas Helmer and midfielders Mario Basler, Dieter Eilts and Christian Ziege they should win, but an Irish victory would keep them in contention for a qualifying place.
The top two teams in group nine meet on Saturday with Portugal needing a win over leaders Ukraine to keep the pressure on Germany, who beat Armenia 5-1 in their opening match.
If Portugal should lose and if Germany win, Portugal will find it extremely tough to finish in the top two.
